text.text: Outbound: how do concurrent Send clicks claim one draft so only one proceeds?

New engineers · The owner's Send click from two tabs, the sendAction server action, and the atomic Postgres claim on one message
row.
Local browser, two tabs of one client

Owner clicks Send
on a draft

Key: frames = trust/deployment zones; box = runtime actor/process; cylinder = stored state. Arrows: caller → recipient,
response included; solid = sync. Flow type is also written on each arrow.

After loadSettings, one UPDATE
WHERE id, direction='out', status IN
(draft,failed) sets sending, clears error,
stamps sentAt/updatedAt, saves edits,
RETURNING. No row → skipped.

After a win, failed guards set the row
to failed or skipped, with sentAt null
and an error. Failed rows can be
claimed again by a manual Send.
Skipped rows cannot.

This only prevents duplicate claims. It
does not guarantee delivery. A row left
'sending' can't be reclaimed. Refresh
resolves only queued LinkedIn rows
that have an externalId.
Outside this view: Post-claim guards, Gmail/LinkedIn delivery and daily rate limits; Finding, research, enrollment and drafting of prospects.
